records.visible_comment: Engineering output in the paper: The 20% SCBA mix exhibited improved sulphate resistance and reduced microstructural deterioration, confirmed by SEM and EDS analyses.
Purpose of the paper: Test whether mechanically processed SCBA can act as an effective supplementary cementitious material that improves strength and durability while reducing environmental impact.
Material-processing method used in the paper: SCBA was oven-dried and sieved through a 300 μm sieve to remove carbon-rich fibrous particles.
Material-processing method used in the paper: Sieved SCBA was ball-milled with 19 mm steel balls at 50 RPM for 180 minutes.
Input used in the focal method: The water-to-binder ratio was fixed at 0.478 for all concrete mixes.
Engineering method used in the paper: Compressive strength was tested on 150 × 150 × 150 mm cubes using a 3000 kN compression testing machine at 14 N/mm² per minute according to IS 516–1959.
Engineering method used in the paper: Splitting tensile strength was tested on 150 × 300 mm cylindrical specimens according to BIS 5816–1999.
Engineering method used in the paper: Flexural strength was evaluated using a three-point loading test according to IS 516:1959.
Engineering method used in the paper: After 28 days of water curing, specimens were exposed for one year to a solution containing 5% sodium sulphate and 5% magnesium sulphate.
Input used in the focal sustainability method: Emission and energy factors were adopted from the Inventory of Carbon and Energy database and previous LCA studies.
System-boundary input used in the focal sustainability method: A cradle-to-gate boundary covering raw-material extraction, transportation, and concrete production at the batching plant.
Environmental sustainability assessment method used in the paper: Inventory of Carbon and Energy datasets were used to assess embodied energy and global warming potential.
Sustainability assessment definition in the paper: Embodied CO₂ is considered equivalent to global warming potential.

Sustainability metric specifications in the paper: Embodied energy is reported in MJ-eq/m³ of concrete, GWP in kg CO₂-eq/m³ of concrete, and Si in kg CO₂-eq/m³ of concrete, preserving the authors' reported units.
Intervention or design choice in the paper: SCBA replacement levels are 0% (CM), 10% (S10), 15% (S15), 20% (S20), and 25% (S25).

Input used in the focal sustainability method: Embodied-energy and GWP characterization factors are specified for diesel, heavy fuel oil, natural gas, cement, sand, processed SCBA, water, and construction.
Sustainability assessment method used in the paper: The sustainability index (Si) of the concrete mixes is calculated using the reported equation.
Engineering-to-sustainability transformation in the paper: The Si calculation combines GWP and 0.050 × embodied energy and normalizes the result by 28-day compressive strength.
Engineering output in the paper: For S20, splitting tensile strength was 2.463 MPa at 7 days and increased progressively over subsequent curing ages.
Engineering output in the paper: For S20, flexural strength increased from 2.92 MPa at 7 days to 4.23, 4.91, 5.20, and 5.41 MPa at 28, 90, 180, and 365 days, respectively.
Engineering method used in the paper: Sulphate resistance was assessed using compressive-strength variation, concrete-cube weight loss, and concrete-prism length change over one year.
Engineering output in the paper: For 20% SCBA, water-cured compressive strengths were 35.02, 41.4, 45.65, and 49.18 MPa, while sulphate-cured specimens reached 34.31, 39.13, 42.29, and 43.73 MPa.
Environmental sustainability outcome in the paper: Embodied energy decreased from 2169.90 MJ-eq/m³ for the control mix to 1778.99 MJ-eq/m³ for S20, an 18.02% reduction.
Engineering output in the paper: At 365 days, S20 reached 49.2 MPa compressive strength compared with 41.4 MPa for the control mix.
Environmental sustainability outcome in the paper: GWP decreased from 318.65 kg CO₂-eq/m³ for the control mix to 259.22 kg CO₂-eq/m³ for S20, an 18.65% reduction.

Environmental sustainability outcome in the paper: S20 achieved a sustainability index of 5.27 kg CO₂-eq/MPa compared with 7.69 kg CO₂-eq/MPa for the control, reported as a 31.5% improvement in resource efficiency.

Environmental sustainability outcome in the paper: S20 achieved an emission-strength efficiency of 5.27 kg CO₂-eq/MPa compared with 7.69 kg CO₂-eq/MPa for the control while reaching 49.2 MPa at 365 days.
Decision or recommendation in the paper: S20 is identified as the most balanced and optimal mix because it combines structural performance with environmental efficiency.

Intervention or design choice in the paper: Mechanically ground, uncalcined SCBA is incorporated as a partial cement replacement and evaluated for mechanical, durability, and sustainability performance.
Sustainability assessment method used in the paper: Sensitivity analysis evaluates how SCBA grinding energy influences embodied energy and GWP results.

Intervention or design choice in the paper: Uncalcined SCBA is used as the replacement material, with the paper noting potentially delayed setting and early-age strength gain because of slower pozzolanic reactivity.
